mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by at least 0.25% over the next month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to turn negative due to tightened financing conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by ≥0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite the FEDFUNDS increase, or the increase is <0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market employment) of at least 2% is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as strong labor demand supports corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2% in the current month
failure_condition: No significant return advantage over a 60-day window when PAYEMS growth is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When both HOUST (industrial production) and RSAFS (retail sales) exceed their prior month levels simultaneously, the S&P 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive, reflecting robust overall demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month AND RSAFS > previous month
failure_condition: 20-day forward return negative despite both HOUST and RSAFS rising.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of more than 5% predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it signals supply-side weakness and potential recession risk.
failure_condition: INDPRO declines by ≤5% or 20-day returns are positive during the decline.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent CPIAUCSL inflation above 3%, the S&P 5-day forward return is expected to be negative as markets anticipate rate hikes.
failure_condition: 5-day forward return positive when CPIAUCSL > 3 for two months.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4.5% for three consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive due to labor market tightening.
failure_condition: 20-day forward return negative despite UNRATE below 4.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monthly increases in GDPC1 (GDP) and HOUST (production) of at least 2% each are associated with a positive S&P 60-day forward return, reflecting strong economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by ≥2% AND HOUST increases by ≥2% in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward return negative despite both proxies rising by ≥2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in GDPC1 (GDP) of 3% or more predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it signals economic contraction and reduced corporate optimism.
failure_condition: 20-day forward return positive during a GDPC1 monthly decline of ≥3%.
